schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE X (A INT, K INT);
CREATE TABLE Y (A INT, K INT);
q1: SELECT X.A AS A FROM X AS X, Y AS Y WHERE X.K = Y.K
q2: SELECT X1.A AS X1A FROM (SELECT X.A AS A, X.K AS K FROM X AS X) AS X1, Y AS Y WHERE X1.K = Y.K
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.A AS A FROM X AS X, Y AS Y WHERE X.K = Y.K
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X1.A AS X1A FROM (SELECT X.A AS A, X.K AS K FROM X AS X) AS X1, Y AS Y WHERE X1.K = Y.K
counterexample: INSERT INTO X (A, K) VALUES (1, 1), (2, 2); INSERT INTO Y (A, K) VALUES (1, 1), (3, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 does not alias the subquery, while Q2 does. This can lead to different results if the subquery in Q2 has duplicate column names.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is triggered when the subquery in Q2 has duplicate column names, which is not allowed in the schema. In Q1, the subquery does not have duplicate column names, so it does not trigger the difference.
